us18_family.topic: Parental leave, childcare and child benefits in Israel and the US

claims.text: NII: maternity allowance daily amount = higher of 3-month income/90 or 6-month income/180, capped at NIS 1,752.33 per day (as of 1 Jan 2026)

NII Annual Survey 2018: maternity insurance in effect from 1 April 1954; allowance 6 or 12 weeks until May 2007, 7 or 14 weeks until end-2016, 8 or 15 weeks from January 2017; paternity entitlement from 1998 when the mother returns to work; 1,266 fathers received it in 2018 (9.5 per 1,000 women); average daily allowance NIS 285 (2018); birth grants 183,877 (2018)

Nefesh B'Nefesh guide: 26 weeks of maternity leave after 12 months with the employer, 15 paid by Bituach Leumi; 8 paid weeks with shorter qualifying work; dismissal protection during pregnancy and 60 days after return, needs a ministerial permit; fertility-treatment absences protected

CRS (26 Mar 2025): FMLA (1993, P.L. 103-3) gives up to 12 weeks of job-protected unpaid leave to eligible workers; 27% of private-industry workers had employer paid family leave in March 2023, about 17 points more than in 2010; 13% in the bottom wage quartile vs 44% in the top; 10 jurisdictions (incl. DC) had active state paid-leave programmes, 4 more enacted (DE, MN Jan 2026; ME May 2026; MD July 2026); California first, 1 July 2004; federal civil-service paid parental leave created by the FY2020 NDAA (Dec 2019)
BLS: 27% of civilian workers had paid family leave and 90% unpaid family leave (March 2023); paid family leave estimates unavailable for 2024 and 2025 due to a change in scope
DOL National Database of Childcare Prices (2022 data, 2,512 counties): full-day care for one child cost $6,552 to $15,600 a year, 8.9% to 16% of county median family income
NII child allowance rates from 1 Jan 2026: NIS 173 for the 1st child, NIS 219 for the 2nd-4th, NIS 173 for the 5th and later

NII 2018: Children Insurance Law from 1959, initially for large families only; allowances cut 2003-04 with children born from June 2003 paid the same rate as the first two until June 2009; Streamlining Law cut allowances in August 2013 (new-child rate NIS 140); raised May 2015 with a savings plan from January 2017 (state NIS 50 a month, parents may add NIS 50); about 1.186m families and 2.88m children received allowances in 2018

Scripps News (Census): the 2021 expanded CTC raised the credit from $2,000 to $3,000 per child ($3,600 under 6); after it returned to normal levels in 2022, SPM child poverty rose from 5.2% (2021) to 12.4% (2022)
OECD PF1.1 (Feb 2025): OECD average public spending on family benefits 2.35% of GDP in 2021; US below 1% of GDP, more than half on services
OECD SOCX public family expenditure (cash and in-kind, excludes tax breaks): Israel 1.886% of GDP in 2023 (series range 1.735-2.493); US 0.767% in 1980 and 0.604% in 2023 (range 0.408-0.846)

us18_reproduction.topic: Abortion, IVF and fertility in Israel and the US

claims.text: 1977 law (Penal Code ss.312-321): termination committees (two physicians and a social worker, at least one woman; 38 committees) may approve where the woman is under 18 (later under 20) or over 40, pregnancy from rape, incest or outside marriage, fetal defect, or risk to life or health; about 98% approved; 19,500 legal abortions in 2003; 9 per 1,000 women of childbearing age in 2016 vs US 13.2; 2014 change put elective abortion in the state-funded basket (sources inconsistent on an age-33 limit); free for soldiers; a 2012 report found about half of abortions in private clinics without committee approval

ToI 27 Jun 2022: Health Minister Nitzan Horowitz eased rules: drug abortions at HMO clinics, no in-person committee appearance, contraception questions dropped, social-worker meeting optional; 'The rights to a woman's body are those of the woman alone'; CBS recorded 16,492 requests in 2020, 99.6% approved; 17,548 requests in 2021 (Ynet); abolishing committees requires legislation

#WeCount (10 Jun 2026): about 1.13 million abortions in the formal health system in 2025; telehealth 29% of abortions by Dec 2025 (25% Dec 2024; 5% Apr 2022); in total-ban states telehealth was 97-100% of abortions in 2025

KFF (24 Jul 2026): Hyde Amendment since 1977 bars federal funds for abortion except life endangerment, rape or incest; 13 states require state-funded Medicaid abortion coverage; 13 states had total bans as of 6 January 2026 (AL, AR, ID, IN, KY, LA, ND, MS, OK, SD, TN, TX, WV)

IJHPR 2016: Israel's national health basket provides practically unlimited IVF to patients under 45 with no more than two children, single mothers included; Israel performs the most IVF cycles per capita in the world; US performed 163,212 IVF cycles in 2013
NCHS: general fertility rate 53.1 per 1,000 women 15-44 in 2025 (provisional), 53.8 in 2024; down 23% since 2007; 3,606,400 births in 2025
AP (24 Jul 2025): US TFR 1.599 in 2024 (record low), 1.621 in 2023; about 2.1 in 2007; Trump administration issued an executive order to expand access to and lower the cost of IVF

us18_safetynet.topic: Pensions, disability, long-term care and social insurance

claims.text: CRS on the 2026 Trustees Report: OASI fund depleted Q4 2032, combined OASDI Q3 2034, after which revenue covers about 83% of scheduled benefits (65% by 2100); over 71 million beneficiaries; 2025 total cost $1,609.5bn; 75-year deficit 4.42% of taxable payroll (3.82% in 2025 report)

Census P60-290: official poverty 10.2% in 2025, 34.5m people; child official poverty a historic low 13.4%; SPM 13.1%, not statistically different from 2024; Social Security moved 28.8 million people out of SPM poverty, the largest anti-poverty programme
Gronau and Spivak: Israel closed the old pension funds to new members in 1995, moved from defined-benefit to defined-contribution pensions, and passed the Mandatory Pension Law of 2008

Taub (Jan 2014): one in five elderly Israelis was poor in the mid-2000s (20.7% on disposable income vs 5.9% across 21 OECD countries, Ben-David and Bleikh 2013); a 2008 order mandated pensions for all salaried employees, at least 17.5% of salary up to the average wage from January 2014, about two-thirds paid by employers; only 24% of the elderly receive the means-tested income supplement; public pensions replace about 22% of an average wage; retirement ages 67 men, 62 women

NII: long-term care reform in force November 2018, levels raised from 3 to 6, choice of cash, hybrid or in-kind care (about 14.5%/57%/28.5%); 309,435 elderly receive the benefit, about 55,000 in serious nursing condition; about 131,400 more people in four years

ToI 13 Feb 2018: Knesset passed 84-0 a NIS 4.3bn ($1.23bn) four-year plan raising disability benefits by NIS 470-770 a month to nearly NIS 4,000; activists sought parity with the minimum wage; Welfare Minister Haim Katz: 'This is the first step to bringing it up to minimum wage.'

us18_poverty.topic: Poverty over time: NII and Census

claims.text: NII 2024: persons 20.7% (20.6% 2023), families 20.0% (20.2%), children 28% (~880,000), about 2 million poor; Arab families 37.6% (38.1%), Haredi families 32.8% (33.0%); 158,700 poor elderly, above the OECD average; poverty line NIS 3,547 per standard person; without NII transfers persons 31.5% and families 34.5%; Israel second in OECD child poverty after Costa Rica; 28.1% food insecure

NII 2023 report: persons 21.9% (2010), 22.3% (2015), 20.1% (2020), 20.8% (2022), 20.7% (2023) (2010-2020 read from chart); elderly 12.8% 2022 and 2023; transfers and taxes cut person poverty by 36.0% (2010), 30.1% (2019), 41.1% (2020), 33.5% (2023); OECD-scale comparison: Israel 19.5% vs OECD average 11.6% (persons), children 23.4% vs 12.4%, 66+ 17.8% vs 15.1%

NII 2018 report: poverty line is 50% of median disposable income per standard person; 2018 persons 21.2%, families 18.0%, children 30.0%, elderly 18.8%; before transfers and taxes persons 28.0%, families 27.8%; series break 2011/2012 (move from income to expenditure surveys)

NII Annual Survey 2007: net-income poverty 2004 families 20.3%, persons 23.6%, children 33.2%, elderly 25.1%; 2006 families 20.0%, persons 24.5%, children 35.8%, elderly 21.5%; child allowance cutback from 2002 raised child poverty by 5 points 2002-2005; income support plus child allowances for a couple with two children fell from about 71% of the poverty line in 2002 to 48.9% in 2006

CRS (16 Sep 2026): official poverty 10.2% in 2025, down from 10.7% the previous year; 34.5m people; child 13.4% (14.4%); SPM 13.1%; thresholds $16,749 (single under 65), $32,649 (two adults, two children)

Stateline (16 Sep 2026): 10.2% is a historic low; median household income $87,460; experts expect worse figures once the 2025 tax and spending law's cuts to Medicaid and food assistance take effect; children receiving SNAP fell 1.2 million July 2025-July 2026 (CBPP)
Contradiction: the US official poverty rate for 2024 appears as 10.6% in the historical table (EPI) and as 10.7% in CRS's comparison with 2025
